problem.text: The change addresses the reported object-filename conflict by separating the CUDA loader's basename from stloader.cpp.

reasoning.text: Renaming stloader.cu to stloader_cu.cu removes the shared stem without merging translation units or changing loader algorithms. This would avoid collisions in build paths that derive object names by replacing the source extension.

impact.text: Both installation-time and JIT builds discover .cu and .cpp sources recursively, so the renamed CUDA file requires no explicit source-list update.

source_notes.text: Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” reports an extension-import failure and a reporter-provided toolchain workaround. Its relationship here is only an inferred shared extension-build context: its traceback names ext.py's import, not a loader object-name collision.

limitations: No build was executed; the affected compiler/backend and its actual object-naming rule are unestablished.
This filename-and-include change offers no useful numerical computation to validate; loader runtime correctness was not tested.

claims.text: The CUDA implementation becomes stloader_cu.cu, and its header becomes stloader_cu.cuh. Both stloader.cpp and the CUDA implementation update their include directives; the header contents remain identical.

The whole-parent-tree search finds precisely these two references to the old header name. The patch updates both, preserving the host/CUDA declaration boundary while changing filesystem names rather than callable interfaces.

setup.py passes discovered sources to CUDAExtension with BuildExtension; ext.py passes its discovered sources to torch.utils.cpp_extension.load when the prebuilt extension is absent. The rename therefore fits both existing discovery mechanisms without changing their selection conditions or compiler flags.

annotation.summary: Renames the CUDA safetensors loader and its header to distinguish them from stloader.cpp, updating includes while retaining automatic build-source discovery.
